scope:
This design covers the canonical RFC 9000 transport slice, including packet forms, stream semantics, frame codecs, transport-parameter handling, version negotiation, and the transport-side recovery contracts surfaced in the requirement file.
The current flow-control slice spans a connection-scoped helper and runtime path for stream opening, ordered receive buffering, final-size accounting, MAX_* credit publication/repair, and bounded final-size-bearing FIN/RESET retransmission preservation.
It does not define RFC 8999 version-independent invariants or RFC 9001 TLS-protection details as separate concerns, and it does not claim full retransmission-driven send states or STOP_SENDING/RESET orchestration.
title: QUIC RFC 9000 Transport Verification
status_summary: Passed on 2026-04-30 for the bounded RFC 9000 transport trace surface. The focused requirement-home and codec/fuzz filter (`FullyQualifiedName~RFC9000|...transport/parser/codec/fuzz classes`) passed 1,682/1,682. Dry benchmark smoke executed `QuicHeaderParsingBenchmarks` (9), `QuicFrameCodecBenchmarks` (12), `QuicStreamParsingBenchmarks` (4), and `QuicVariableLengthIntegerBenchmarks` (8). A same-day idle-timeout follow-up added focused `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S18P2-0002` proof that public `TimeSpan` idle-timeout values are encoded as RFC 9000 `max_idle_timeout` milliseconds on the wire and converted to runtime microseconds only after transport-parameter commit. A 2026-05-01 stream-retransmission follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S13P3-0001` through `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S13P3-0005`, showing lost STREAM information rebuilt into a new protected packet and retained only until the relevant packet is acknowledged. A 2026-05-01 CRYPTO discard follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S13P3-0007` proof that Initial and Handshake CRYPTO retransmission data is removed when the corresponding packet number space is discarded while other spaces are retained. A 2026-05-01 stream-control follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P5-0004` proof that a valid STOP_SENDING request produces RESET_STREAM state and an invalid peer-unidirectional STOP_SENDING does not create a reset request. A 2026-05-01 STOP_SENDING state follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P5-0005` proof that Ready, Send, and bidirectional send-side streams emit RESET_STREAM on STOP_SENDING while invalid peer-unidirectional requests are rejected. A 2026-05-01 retransmission-priority follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S13P3-0034` proof that later application stream writes are queued behind pending Application Data STREAM retransmissions when no application priority override exists. A 2026-05-01 STOP_SENDING retransmission follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P5-0011` proof that a lost STOP_SENDING is flushed as a new protected Application Data packet preserving the original stream and error fields while unrelated ACKs do not suppress the queued retry. A 2026-05-01 Data Sent STOP_SENDING follow-up added direct `RFC9000-S3-5-P4-S3-R01` proof that Data Sent streams can emit RESET_STREAM with the established final size, acknowledged Data Sent streams reject later STOP_SENDING without creating a reset, and bidirectional Data Sent resets leave the receive side live. A 2026-05-01 STOP_SENDING error-code follow-up added direct `RFC9000-S3-5-P5-S1-R01` proof that accepted STOP_SENDING copies the application error code into RESET_STREAM and send-abort state, rejected STOP_SENDING does not synthesize or store a copied reset error, and the copy path preserves the maximum QUIC varint application error code. A 2026-05-01 peer-reset STOP_SENDING follow-up added direct `RFC9000-S3-5-P6-S1-R01` proof that local read-abort requests do not emit STOP_SENDING after the peer has reset the receive direction, while peer STOP_SENDING is accepted before peer reset and rejected after peer reset. A 2026-05-01 bidirectional RESET_STREAM follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P5-0012` proof that local write abort can terminate only the send direction of a bidirectional stream with RESET_STREAM state while invalid peer-initiated bidirectional write aborts are rejected. A 2026-05-01 STOP_SENDING prompt-termination follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P5-0013` proof that local read abort emits a protected STOP_SENDING frame carrying the requested application error code and does not emit RESET_STREAM or write-aborted notifications. A 2026-05-01 S3P3 delayed-frame follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P3-0003`, `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P3-0004`, and `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S3P3-0006` proof that delayed receive-side state-changing frames are accepted after Data Recvd, MAX_STREAM_DATA is emitted while the receive side remains Recv, and delayed MAX_STREAM_DATA plus STOP_SENDING are accepted after Data Sent. A 2026-05-02 S4P2 repeated-credit follow-up added direct `RFC9000-S4-2-P2-S1-R01` edge proof that MAX_DATA and MAX_STREAM_DATA advertisements can advance to the maximum QUIC varint flow-control limit without overflow while duplicate maximum advertisements leave the limit unchanged. A 2026-05-02 S4P2 opportunistic-credit follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S4P2-0003` proof that no credit frames are created when no application bytes are read, and partial reads publish only the credit unlocked by consumed bytes. A 2026-05-02 S4P1 non-increasing MAX-frame follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0174` proof that increasing MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAM_DATA frames advance send limits while non-increasing frames are ignored without changing the accepted limits. A 2026-05-02 S4P1 limit-advertisement follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S4P1-0001` negative and edge proof that duplicate received bytes do not inflate advertised receive limits and gapped data does not publish credit until contiguous application bytes are consumable. A 2026-05-02 S4P1 per-stream receive-limit follow-up added direct `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S4P1-0002` positive, negative, and edge proof that receive-stream accounting is bounded per stream, one stream cannot consume the whole connection receive buffer, and consuming one stream advances only that stream's receive limit. A 2026-05-03 Retry-cardinality follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-1033`, `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-1034`, and `RFC9000-S17-2-5-1-P3-S3-R01`, with `QuicListenerHost` now issuing Retry in response to Initial and 0-RTT datagrams, reusing stored Retry state for follow-up datagrams, and preserving the single-datagram one-Retry floor after a Release build and targeted test run. A 2026-05-03 future-IETF reserved-range follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0898`, with `QuicVersionNegotiation` now exposing a top-16-bit reserved-range classifier and the Release build / targeted requirement-home test passing. A 2026-05-03 closing-state reply follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `RFC9000-S10-2-1-P5-R01`, showing the Closing-phase path replies to arbitrary UDP datagrams with CONNECTION_CLOSE while the Draining phase does not. A 2026-05-03 close-state retain-keys follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `RFC9000-S10-2-1-P4-S3-R01`, showing the Closing-phase path retains 1-RTT open material long enough to read and process a peer CONNECTION_CLOSE frame while non-close protected packets still get the local close reply. A 2026-05-03 close-state send-rate follow-up added direct requirement-home proof for `RFC9000-S10-2-1-P3-S1-R01`, showing the Closing-phase reply window is bounded by the close lifetime and packets after expiry no longer trigger a close reply. A 2026-05-07 S7P2 follow-up added focused requirement-home proof for `REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0305` and `RFC9000-S7-2-P2-S2-R01`, and regenerated coverage triage now marks both trace_clean. BenchmarkDotNet reported expected Dry minimum-iteration-time warnings, so the benchmark evidence proves suite execution only and is not a performance claim. Full sender/recovery orchestration and broad STOP_SENDING/RESET orchestration remain outside this umbrella except where separately traced.
